security_audit.summary: Static scanner alerts are mostly false positives from Markdown code examples, JavaScript template literals, static imports, and normal environment configuration. I found no prompt injection or evidence of malicious installer behavior. One semantic issue remains: an update repository example constructs SQL identifiers from unvalidated update fields.

remediation.issue: Dynamic SQL update fields are built from Object.keys(updates).
remediation.suggestion: Replace the example with an allowlist that maps accepted DTO fields to fixed SQL column names before constructing the SET clause.

remediation.issue: The documentation does not warn readers about identifier interpolation in SQL examples.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short note that SQL values must be parameterized and SQL identifiers must come from trusted constants or allowlisted mappings.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Dynamic SQL Column Construction
semantic_findings.description: The repository update example builds a SQL SET clause from Object.keys(updates) and injects field names into the query. Values are parameterized, but column names are not allowlisted, so copied code could permit SQL injection or mass assignment through unexpected update keys.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly interpolates field names from an updates object into SQL. The values are parameterized, but the identifiers are dynamic and there is no allowlist in the example.

content.value_statement: Node.js backend projects need consistent architecture, security, and database patterns. This skill guides Express and Fastify services with practical examples and review checklists.
actual_capabilities: Explains Express and Fastify server setup with common middleware.
Outlines layered architecture with controllers, services, and repositories.
Shows authentication, validation, error handling, logging, and rate limiting patterns.
Covers PostgreSQL, MongoDB, transactions, Redis caching, and JWT flows.
Provides testing, response format, and production best-practice guidance.
limitations: It is guidance only; it does not run code or generate a full repository by itself.
Examples require security review before use in production.
It does not replace framework documentation or threat modeling.
It does not cover every Node.js framework or deployment platform.

use_cases.title: Design a REST API
use_cases.description: Plan routes, middleware, validation, response formats, and service layers for a new Express or Fastify API.

use_cases.title: Standardize Service Architecture
use_cases.description: Create shared patterns for controllers, repositories, error handling, logging, and database access across a team.

use_cases.title: Review Backend Scaffolding
use_cases.description: Check generated Node.js backend code for missing validation, authentication, transactions, and production safeguards.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Backend API
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Node.js backend patterns skill to plan a REST API for my product. Include routes, middleware, data models, validation, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design Service Layers
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to design controllers, services, repositories, and dependency injection for this feature. Explain each layer and its responsibilities.

prompt_templates.title: Review Authentication Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to review my JWT authentication and refresh token design. Identify missing validation, secret handling, rate limits, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Production Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to create a production readiness checklist for my Node.js backend. Cover logging, database connections, caching, testing, deployment, and security controls.

output_examples.input: Design a user management API with Express, PostgreSQL, and JWT authentication.
output: A route plan for registration, login, profile reads, updates, and deletion.
A layered architecture with controller, service, repository, and validation responsibilities.
Security notes for password hashing, token expiry, rate limiting, and error responses.

output_examples.input: Review an existing Fastify service before production release.
output: A review checklist covering middleware, schema validation, logging, and database pooling.
A list of missing production controls and suggested remediation steps.
A testing plan for routes, services, repositories, and error paths.

output_examples.input: Add Redis caching to a Node.js backend service.
output: A caching strategy that defines keys, time to live, invalidation, and failure behavior.
Guidance for rate limiting and cache client configuration.
Operational notes for monitoring cache errors and avoiding stale data.

best_practices: Validate request bodies, query parameters, and route parameters before service logic runs.
Keep controllers thin and place business rules in services with tested repository boundaries.
Load secrets from managed configuration and avoid logging sensitive values.
anti_patterns: Do not mix HTTP handling, business rules, and database queries in one route handler.
Do not build SQL identifiers from request data without an allowlist.
Do not expose raw errors or stack traces in production responses.

faq.question: What frameworks does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Express and Fastify patterns for Node.js backend services.

faq.question: Can it generate a complete backend project?
faq.answer: It can guide structure and implementation, but generated code still needs local testing and review.

faq.question: Does it include database guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes PostgreSQL, MongoDB, transactions, connection pooling, and repository patterns.

faq.question: Does it help with authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes JWT authentication, refresh tokens, password hashing, middleware, and authorization checks.

faq.question: Is it only for REST APIs?
faq.answer: No. It is most detailed for REST APIs, but the architecture guidance also supports GraphQL and services.

faq.question: What should users review before production?
faq.answer: Users should review validation, secret handling, SQL construction, logging, rate limits, tests, and deployment settings.
